claim: Let \(k\) be algebraically closed of characteristic \(2\), let \(A=E\times E\) be the superspecial abelian surface in Schröer’s model, let \(T=A/\{\pm1\}\), and let \(T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{(x^2,y^2,z)}T\) be the crepant partial resolution at its singular point. If \(\nu:S\to T'\) is the normalization and \(F\cong\mathbb P^1\oplus\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)\) is the exceptional fiber, then the normalization-defect sheaf is \(\nu_*\mathcal O_S/\mathcal O_{T'}\cong i_*\pi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)\), where \(i:F\hookrightarrow T'\) and \(\pi:F\to F_{\mathrm{red}}\cong\mathbb P^1\). Consequently it has filtration \(0\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-2)\to\pi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)\to0\), and \(h^1(F,\pi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1))=1\).

correctness.rationale: The chart ring map is explicit. On the \(x^2\)-chart, \(S_x=R_x[t]\), \(t^2=q\), and \(S_x/R_x\) is generated by \([t]\). The annihilator contains \((x,r^2)\), and reduction modulo \(x\) identifies \(R_x/(x,r^2)\) with \(k[q,r]/(r^2)\), embedded into \(k[t,r]/(r^2)\) by \(q=t^2\); multiplication by \(t\) has image in the odd \(t\)-parity summand, proving injectivity. The symmetric \(y^2\)-chart has transition \(q^{-1}\); the \(z\)-chart misses the exceptional fiber. The \(\mathbb P^1\) cohomology sequence yields \(h^1=1\).

originality.rationale: The inspected primary text proves nonnormality, identifies the common normalization and conductor, and describes the conductor image and Frobenius map on reduced fibers. It does not state the full quotient sheaf as the pullback of \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)\), nor its filtration and \(h^1\). Searches surfaced only normalization/conductor results for different objects; this supports a narrow best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: The historical sources cited by Schröer, including Artin’s work on wild involutions and Katsura’s work on Kummer surfaces in characteristic two, were not independently read in full during this run; an equivalent normalization-module calculation there remains possible.
Semantic search is not exhaustive and cannot establish absolute novelty.
